key_insight: GITIII is a lightweight, self-supervised graph transformer that infers cell–cell interactions at single-cell spatial resolution and quantifies how neighbouring cells influence a receiver cell's gene expression in an interpretable way.
problem_solved: Existing spatial transcriptomics models struggle to infer and quantify directional, single-cell-level niche effects while remaining interpretable and computationally efficient; GITIII addresses this by jointly learning cell state and niche correlations with an interpretable transformer.
method: Self-supervised graph transformer that embeds cells in a spatial graph and learns interactions without dense supervision.
Attention-based interpretability to decompose and quantify neighbour-to-receiver influences on gene expression.
Lightweight architecture optimized for single-cell spatial data to enable scalable, per-cell influence scoring and downstream analysis.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with an efficient, interpretable framework for modeling spatially structured biological data, enabling mechanistic insight, hypothesis generation, and integration into downstream pipelines for spatial omics and graph-based biological inference.
visual_elements: Schematic of spatial graph input → graph transformer → per-cell influence scores (node and edge visualization).
Tissue map overlay showing cells colored by predicted receiver gene expression with arrows/weights indicating influential neighbours.
Attention heatmap or bar chart highlighting top neighbour contributors for example receiver cells and target genes.
Flowchart comparing self-supervised training and interpretation pipeline (data → model → influence quantification → biological insight).
paper_title: Inferring spatial single-cell-level interactions through interpreting cell state and niche correlations learned by self-supervised graph transformer
paper_authors: Xiao Xiao, Le Zhang, Hongyu Zhao, Zuoheng Wang
